messages:
maria: Avena (prospect) wants a short validation before we move to contract. Target: sustain 1.2k req/s steady, support bursts to 3k for ~5m, avg response ~200 tokens. p95 target <= 500ms. They asked for a cost ballpark and any security blockers up-front. Meeting Friday.
kevin: Clarify: prompt size? single-turn or chat? hosted vs dedicated preference?
maria: Single-turn prompts, avg prompt ~180 tokens. They're open to hosted but explicitly asked to see a Dedicated baseline for pricing.
alex: I can run the bench. Proposed quick plan:
- Warmup 8m to 400 rps
- Incremental ramps: 400 -> 800 -> 1.2k -> 2k -> 3k (5 min steps)
- Sustain 10m at 1.2k, short 5m spike to 3k
- Capture p50/p95/p99, error rate, CPU/GPU util, kernel stalls
Variants: model=13B-q4 / 34B-q4; batch=[8,12], kv_cache on/off
Add headers: X-Request-Id, X-Prompt-Tokens, X-Response-Tokens
sam: I'll coordinate infra. Suggest running on perf-bench cluster with mixed instance types so we can show both latency-optimized and cost-optimized configs.
ops-bot: loadgen perf-run-141 queued, cluster=perf-bench-east, workers=48, start_eta=60s
alex: k6 snippet (pseudo):
```bash
import http from 'k6/http'
export default function() {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({model:'34B-q4', input:'<...>', max_tokens:200}), { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${__ENV.KEY}` } })
}
```
Also curl example for manual smoke:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"13B-q4","input":"hello","max_tokens":200,"batch_size":8}'
```
zoe: Smoke results from first pass (13B-q4, batch=12, kv_cache off): p50=160ms, p95=610ms, p99=980ms, errors 1.4% (timeouts at 2k-3k spike). Observed queueing at worker ingress during 2k->3k.
kevin: p95 too high for target. Try batch=8 and lower worker concurrency.
alex: Rerun (13B-q4, batch=8): p50=210ms, p95=480ms, p99=760ms, errors 0.3%. Sustained 1.2k for 10m stable. Spike to 3k produced transient errors but recovered.
sam: 34B-q4 (batch=8) results: p50=200ms, p95=430ms, p99=690ms, errors 0.2%. Fewer GPUs for same throughput but more memory pressure per host.
kevin: Cost sketch for proposal (very rough):
- Hosted: estimated monthly run cost for steady 1.2k rps, avg 200 tokens -> ~$28k/mo (includes infra + platform margin). Bursting increases hourly infra but overall ~+15% on avg.
- Dedicated: reserved fleet (~6-8 A100-equivalent) amortized -> infra ~$18k/mo + platform fee -> customer quote ~ $26k/mo with SLA 99.9%. Dedicated has better tail for p95.
maria: Security asks from Avena: SSO integration, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 report, VPC peering. Any blockers?
security-bot: SOC2 PDF link: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf ; KMS: we support CMEK via AWS KMS and GCP KMS; need to schedule key rotation test. VPC peering available for Dedicated; hosted requires IP allowlist and private endpoints (request through infra team).
zoe: Note: during runs we saw KV cache hit rate ~8% for Avena prompt set (very high-variance inputs) so caching won't move the needle.
alex: Recommendation to sales deck:
- Show 2 configs: latency-optimized (34B-q4, batch8) and cost-optimized (13B-q4, batch12)
- Include one-line guidance: expected p95 at 1.2k = 430ms (latency cfg) vs 610ms (cost cfg)
- Include cost ranges and note dedicated reduces tail and gives SLA
maria: Great. Can someone paste the grafana snapshots and raw logs into the meeting invite? Also need an ops bullet: expected failover behavior if a shard hits OOM.
sam: Uploaded artifacts to perf/1829001234/ (grafana, logs, run-metadata). OOM behavior: autoscaler will route to spare hosts, if not available we throttle and surface 503s; will include fallback to smaller model variant if enabled.
kevin: Action items: alex final run summary and single-slide numbers by Thu noon; sam prepare dedicated sizing & quote by Thu EOD; security-bot provide KMS checklist + SOC2 link (done). Maria to book Fri demo.
maria: Thanks all. I'll send a 1-pager to Avena ahead of the call and attach the artifacts. :rocket:
